summary: The article accurately describes the new UPI transaction rules, including MDR for P2M transactions above ₹2,000, the cap for high-value transactions, and flat MDR for essential sectors. The dates and legal basis for these changes are also correctly stated.

claims.claim: When you pay a shop or business (Person-to-Merchant or P2M) using UPI, transactions up to ₹2,000 are still free for the merchant.
claims.note: P2M transactions up to ₹2,000 are exempt from MDR.

claims.claim: For P2M payments above ₹2,000, a small fee called Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) will apply to the merchant.
claims.note: A nominal MDR of 0.4% will be levied on P2M transactions above ₹2,000.

claims.claim: This MDR is a nominal 0.4% of the transaction value, capped at ₹300 for very large transactions (₹75,000 and above).
claims.note: The MDR is 0.4% of the transaction value, capped at ₹300 for transactions of ₹75,000 and above.

claims.claim: The Central Government issued a notification on September 14, 2026, under an amended Payment and Settlement Systems (PSS) Act, 2007.
claims.note: The Central Government issued a notification on September 14, 2026, under the amended Payment and Settlement Systems (PSS) Act, 2007.

claims.claim: Following this, the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) — the organisation that developed and manages UPI — issued a detailed circular on September 15, 2026.
claims.note: NPCI issued a detailed circular on September 15, 2026, outlining the operational details.

claims.claim: Certain essential sectors like railways, telecom, insurance, fuel, and agriculture inputs will have a flat MDR of ₹5 per transaction for amounts above ₹2,000.
claims.note: Railways, telecom, insurance, fuel sectors, agriculture inputs etc. will pay a flat MDR of ₹5 per transaction above ₹2,000.

article_title: Your UPI Payments Just Got a Small Update: What the New Rules Mean
